::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** March 3d [1887?]  
**From:** Elderfield, Otterbourne, Winchester.  
**Manuscript:** MS Charlotte Mitchell
:::

My dear [Edith](people/person_749.qmd)

I want to tell the [SSW](organizations/other_47.qmd) of a lovely book that has been sent to [Gertrude](people/person_1462.qmd) by another invalid.[^1]   It is called '[the Sermon in the Hospital](other_books/otherbook_1023.qmd)', and can be had from Kegan Paul for 3d or 20s for 25 copies.  It is in blank verse and is an extract from a poem by a Mrs Hamilton King, called the Disciples  I am sorry to say they were [Mazzini](people/person_2368.qmd)'s disciples but that does not prevent this Sermon from being a most beautiful thing [^2] 

yours affectionately
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: The Society of Watchers and Workers, founded by Edith Jacob.
[^2]: Harriet (Baillie-Hamilton) King, *The Disciples*  (London: King 1873) was a verse account of J. Ruffini, Ugo Bassi, A. Milano and  Baron G. Nicotera; an extract was published as *The Sermon in the Hospital* (London: Kegan Paul 1887).
